problems.source_says: Another candidate, c594 (Urban, Lukavský, Brom, Hein, Svacha, Děchtěrenko and Urban, 2025, 'Prompting for creative problem-solving: A process-mining study', Learning and Instruction 99, 102156), analyzes the same 77 people as the c123 experimental arm. Its sample matches c123 Table 1 for that arm on N, sex (24 men, 53 women), mean age 22.4, subject (57/17/3), and level (53 undergraduate, 24 graduate). Codebook sections 2 and 8 say papers that analyze the same participants share a sample and get one sample_id, so both records should name each other. c123 was written first and cannot state this, but check (d) covers other papers. c594 has no no-AI arm, so no pooled estimate is at risk today. c594 is not in retrieval.json. I read its PsyArXiv preprint. It also says all 77 used ChatGPT and that prompt logs exist, which answers two of the form's open questions.

confirmed.statement: Volunteers were randomly assigned as individuals to the control or the ChatGPT condition before the experiment. The paper has one study.
S1 n_analyzed = 145, with arms of 77 (experimental) and 68 (control). These are people: 'university students' in the text, N in the Table 1 headers, and students in the abstract.
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Participants and Table 1; p. 2, abstract (page images)

confirmed.statement: Every Table 1 block sums to the arm size: sex 22 + 46 = 68 and 24 + 53 = 77, subject 52 + 9 + 7 and 57 + 17 + 3, level 55 + 13 and 53 + 24, and prior ChatGPT experience 68 and 77.
No exclusions. All participants passed the attention checks and completed all the required tasks. c594 says the same for the 77 experimental participants.

No attrition or missing data in any analysis. Every t-test in Tables 1 and 2 has df 143 (145 minus 2). Every between-group ANCOVA has F(1,142) (145 minus 3, one covariate). The within-experimental self-efficacy test has F(1,75) (77 minus 2).
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Table 1; p. 16, Table 2 and H1 text; p. 17; pp. 19-22

confirmed.statement: The arm sizes reproduce the printed statistics. With n = 68 and 77 and the Table 2 means and SDs, pooled-SD d is 0.70, 0.61, and 0.55 and t is 4.18, 3.65, and 3.28 for quality, elaboration, and originality. The paper prints 0.69, 0.61, 0.55 and 4.16, 3.65, 3.32. So each outcome is one score per person, not per idea or rating.

confirmed.statement: participants.who matches the PDF: 22 male and 46 female vs 24 and 53, mean age 22.5 (SD 4.9) vs 22.4 (SD 4.1), subject 52/9/7 vs 57/17/3, 55 BA and 13 MA vs 53 and 24, a pool of approx. 8000 students, the 'Creative Thinking' email, course credit, and a sample homogenous in race and ethnicity.
The a priori power analysis asked for at least 57 per group. Both arms exceed it.

No other primary paper among the candidates reuses these participants except c594. Three synthesis candidates cite Urban et al. 2024 in their reference lists. They are reference-list records under codebook section 3, not shared samples.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 145 people analyzed, and each arm alone is above 50. The reuse of the 77 in c594 does not change this.

summary: The participant counts hold: one randomized study analyzed 145 students (77 with ChatGPT, 68 without) with no exclusions, and the Table 1 sums, the df of 143 and 142, and the printed t and d values all agree with those arm sizes, so criterion 2 is met on S1 alone. The coding is refuted on sample_overlap, which is empty although c594 (Urban et al. 2025, Learning and Instruction 99, 102156) says it analyzes the same 77 experimental participants, and three minor items also need fixing: country (Czech Republic, per c594), the locator for the Ns in one_line_finding, and a note that wrongly says the markdown stops at p. 23.
